context.title: Abner Changes Sides
context.summary: As David grows stronger, Abner quarrels with Ish-bosheth and offers to bring all Israel over to David. David demands his wife Michal back. Joab, avenging his brother, murders Abner at Hebron's gate, and David publicly mourns him.
context.background: Taking a king's concubine was a claim on his throne, which is why Ish-bosheth's accusation (v. 7) was so serious (compare 16:21-22). Hebron was a city of refuge (Joshua 20:7), making Joab's private revenge in its gate especially shocking. Absalom's mother was a princess of Geshur (v. 3).

customs.note: Saul had given Michal to another man after David fled (1 Samuel 25:44). Her second husband follows her, weeping, until Abner sends him home.

watchFor: 'David waxed stronger and stronger, and the house of Saul waxed weaker' (v. 1).
David's public grief convinces the people he had no part in the murder (vv. 31–37).
'These men the sons of Zeruiah be too hard for me' (v. 39).

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Amnon
people.summary: The eldest son of David, by Ahinoam of Jezreel (1 Chr. 3:1; 2 Sam. 3:2).

people.name: Ahinoam
people.summary: A Jezreelitess, the first wife of David (1 Sam. 25:43; 27:3). She was the mother of Amnon (2 Sam. 3:2).

people.name: Absalom
people.summary: Father of peace; i.e., “peaceful” David’s son by Maacah (2 Sam. 3:3; comp. 1 Kings 1:6). He was noted for his personal beauty and for the extra-ordinary profusion of the hair of his head (2 Sam. 14:25,26).

people.name: Nabal
people.summary: Foolish, a descendant of Caleb who dwelt at Maon (1 Sam. 25), the modern Main, 7 miles south-east of Hebron. He was “very great, and he had 3,000 sheep and 1,000 goats...but the man was churlish and evil in his doings.”

people.name: Abigail
people.summary: The wife of the churlish Nabal, who dwelt in the district of Carmel (1 Sam. 25:3). She showed great prudence and delicate management at a critical period of her husband’s life.

people.name: Talmai
people.summary: A king of Geshur, to whom Absalom fled after he had put Amnon to death (2 Sam. 3:3; 13:37).

people.name: Daniel
people.summary: David’s second son, “born unto him in Hebron, of Abigail the Carmelitess” (1 Chr. 3:1).

people.name: Maacah
people.summary: A daughter of Talmai, king of the old native population of Geshur.

people.name: Adonijah
people.summary: The fourth son of David (2 Sam. 3:4). After the death of his elder brothers, Amnon and Absalom, he became heir-apparent to the throne. But Solomon, a younger brother, was preferred to him.

people.name: Haggith
people.summary: Festive; the dancer, a wife of David and the mother of Adonijah (2 Sam. 3:4; 1 Kings 1:5, 11; 2:13; 1 Chr. 3:2), who, like Absalom, was famed for his beauty.

people.name: Abital
people.summary: Father of dew; i.e., “fresh”, David’s fifth wife (2 Sam. 3:4).

people.name: Eglah
people.summary: A heifer, one of David’s wives, and mother of Ithream (2 Sam. 3:5; 1 Chr. 3:3).

people.name: Abner
people.summary: Father of light; i.e., “enlightening”, the son of Ner and uncle of Saul. He was commander-in-chief of Saul’s army (1 Sam. 14:50; 17:55; 20:25).

people.name: Ish-bosheth
people.summary: Man of shame or humiliation, the youngest of Saul’s four sons, and the only one who survived him (2 Sam. 2-4). His name was originally Eshbaal (1 Chr. 8:33; 9:39).

people.name: Rizpah
people.summary: Coal; hot stone, the daughter of Aiah, and one of Saul’s concubines.

people.name: Judah
people.summary: Praise, the fourth son of Jacob by Leah.

people.name: Dan
people.summary: The fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s maid (Gen. 30:6, “God hath judged me”, Heb. dananni).

people.name: Saul
people.summary: The son of Kish (probably his only son, and a child of prayer, “asked for”), of the tribe of Benjamin, the first king of the Jewish nation. The singular providential circumstances connected with his election as king are recorded in 1 Sam. 8-10.

people.name: Michal
people.summary: Rivulet, or who as God?, the younger of Saul’s two daughters by his wife Ahinoam (1 Sam. 14:49, 50). “Attracted by the graces of his person and the gallantry of his conduct, she fell in love with David and became his wife” (18:20-28).

people.name: Laish
people.summary: The father of Phalti (1 Sam. 25:44).

people.name: Phaltiel
people.summary: Deliverance of the Lord, the son of Laish of Gallim (1 Sam. 25:44)= Phaltiel (2 Sam. 3:15).

people.name: Benjamin
people.summary: The younger son of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 35:18). His birth took place at Ephrath, on the road between Bethel and Bethlehem, at a short distance from the latter place.

people.name: Joab
people.summary: One of the three sons of Zeruiah, David’s sister, and “captain of the host” during the whole of David’s reign (2 Sam. 2:13; 10:7; 11:1; 1 Kings 11:15).

people.name: Ner
people.summary: Light, the father of Kish (1 Chr. 8:33). 1 Sam. 14:51 should be read, “Kish, the father of Saul, and Ner, the father of Abner, were the sons of Abiel.”

people.name: Asahel
people.summary: Made by God, the youngest son of Zeruiah, David’s sister. He was celebrated for his swiftness of foot. When fighting against Ish-bosheth at Gibeon, in the army of his brother Joab, he was put to death by Abner, whom he pursued from the field of battle (2 Sam. 2:18, 19).

people.name: Abishai
people.summary: Father of (i.e., “desirous of”) a gift, the eldest son of Zeruiah, David’s sister. He was the brother of Joab and Asahel (2 Sam. 2:18; 1 Chr. 2:16).

people.name: Zeruiah
people.summary: Stricken of the Lord, David’s sister, and the mother of Abishai, Joab, and Asahel (1 Chr. 2:16), who were the three leading heroes of David’s army, and being his nephews, they were admitted to the closest companionship with him.

places.name: Hebron
places.summary: A city in the south end of the valley of Eshcol, about midway between Jerusalem and Beersheba, from which it is distant about 20 miles in a straight line.

places.name: Jezreel
places.summary: A town in Judah (Josh. 15:56), to the south-east of Hebron.

places.name: Carmel
places.summary: A town in the hill country of Judah (Josh. 15:55), the residence of Nabal (1 Sam. 25:2, 5, 7, 40), and the native place of Abigail, who became David’s wife (1 Sam. 27:3).

places.name: Geshur
places.summary: Bridge, the name of a district or principality of Syria near Gilead, between Mount Hermon and the Lake of Tiberias (2 Sam. 15:8; 1 Chr. 2:23).

places.name: Beersheba
places.summary: Well of the oath, or well of seven, a well dug by Abraham, and so named because he and Abimelech here entered into a compact (Gen. 21:31). On re-opening it, Isaac gave it the same name (Gen. 26:31-33).

places.name: Dan
places.summary: The fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s maid (Gen. 30:6, “God hath judged me”, Heb. dananni).

places.name: Bahurim
places.summary: Young men, a place east of Jerusalem (2 Sam. 3:16; 19:16), on the road to the Jordan valley.

places.name: Sirah
places.summary: Retiring, a well from which Joab’s messenger brought back Abner (2 Sam. 3:26).

places.name: Gibeon
places.summary: Hill-city, “one of the royal cities, greater than Ai, and all the men thereof were mighty” (Josh. 10:2). Its inhabitants were Hivites (11:19).

events.title: Reign of David
events.summary: Passage: 2 Samuel 2:1–24:25. People: David. Place: Hebron, Jerusalem. Lasted about 40 years.
